mac.title: macOS App
mac.lead: Mirror any window or screen region into floating on-top windows.
mac.brew.hint: Run these commands to install (automatic updates handled by Sparkle afterwards):
mac.dl.1: Unzip and drag MagicMirror.app into your Applications folder.
mac.dl.2: First launch: right-click the app → Open → Open.
mac.dl.3: Grant Screen Recording permission in System Settings → Privacy & Security, then relaunch.
mac.f1: Pick any open window or screen region and get an instant floating picture-in-picture overlay.
mac.f2: One floating window per mirror / grouped per app / everything in a single unified window.
mac.f3: Scroll on the mirror to zoom (0.25×–8×) with aspect-preserving resize.
mac.f4: Toggle to click straight through the floating window and interact with what's behind.
mac.f5: Adjust 1–60 FPS per mirror to balance smoothness and resources.
mac.f6: Show or hide all mirrors with a configurable shortcut from any app.
mac.req: Requires macOS 26.0+ (Tahoe). Screen Recording permission is needed on first use.
mac.privacy.d: All frames are processed locally — no frame data is uploaded or stored.
mac.privacy.sentry: Only when the app crashes, an anonymous diagnostic report (crash stack and OS version) is sent to Sentry to help fix issues; it never contains any frame content. See the privacy policy.
usage.title: Usage Guide
usage.lead: From your first mirror to managing multiple pages — up and running in minutes.
usage.s1: Click the Magic Mirror icon in the browser toolbar to open the panel.
usage.s2: Click Start Mirroring to enter selection mode (elements highlight as you hover).
usage.s3: Click the element you want — a floating picture-in-picture window appears, showing that area live.
usage.s4: Press <kbd>Esc</kbd> (or click Start Mirroring again) to exit selection; the mirror keeps running.
usage.s5: Click a tile in the floating window (or the source element again) to remove that mirror; closing the window stops everything.
usage.w1: Scroll to zoom: hover a tile and scroll up to zoom in, down to zoom out (0.25×–8×).
usage.w2: Zoom badge: hovering a tile shows the current zoom factor in its corner.
usage.w3: Remove: click a tile to remove that mirror.
usage.w4: Source label: tiles from other pages show their source domain in the corner.
usage.multi: Put content from multiple pages into one window
usage.multi.d: Chrome allows only one PiP window globally, but you can share it across pages:
usage.m1: On page A (e.g. OKX) pick a balance element — the window appears and page A becomes the host.
usage.m2: Switch to page B (e.g. TradingView), click the icon → Start Mirroring → pick the price element.
usage.m3: Page B's content joins page A's window automatically — both update live, side by side.
usage.m4: A 3rd, 4th… any number of pages can do the same; each contributes one tile.
usage.multi.note: Note: each page contributes at most one element; changes in the source page sync live; background tabs may capture at a lower frame rate.
usage.ms.d: By default each page keeps one mirror; picking again replaces it. To mirror several elements on the same page, enable multi-select mode in the options page (popup → Settings, or chrome://extensions → Magic Mirror → Details → Extension options). Selection stays active so you can pick multiple elements sharing one window.
usage.n1: HTTPS required: mirroring uses tab capture, so pages must be HTTPS (Chrome requirement).
usage.n2: Visible area: only the visible page area is captured; if an element scrolls out of view the tile shows a placeholder and resumes automatically when it's back.
usage.n3: Privacy: everything is processed locally in your browser — nothing is uploaded or stored. See the privacy policy.
usage.install.store: Now available on the Chrome Web Store: install Magic Mirror.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.lead.1: Magic Mirror respects your privacy. This policy explains what information the Chrome extension and the macOS app access, and how it is handled.
privacy.summary: In one sentence: frame content is processed entirely locally — this product never collects, stores, uploads, or sells your screen data. The only exception is anonymous diagnostic information sent when the macOS app crashes (see below), which never contains frame content.
privacy.products.d: This policy applies to both products:
privacy.products.1: Chrome Extension (Magic Mirror) — mirrors regions of webpages into a floating window inside Chrome.
privacy.products.2: macOS App (Magic Mirror) — mirrors any window or screen region into a floating on-top window.
privacy.screen.d: When you create a mirror, the product reads the rendered pixels of the selected area to display them in the floating window.
privacy.screen.1: This data is used only to draw the mirror you requested and is processed in memory only.
privacy.screen.2: Captured frames are processed locally on your device and are never uploaded, stored, or transmitted anywhere.
privacy.screen.3: The product cannot read page DOM, form data, or clipboard content, and never persists any frames.
privacy.tabs.d: When you combine content from multiple pages into one window, the extension reads the title/URL of joining tabs, solely to label the source on mirror tiles. This is used for on-screen labels only and is never stored or transmitted.
privacy.storage.d: The extension stores settings locally in the browser (e.g. the multi-select toggle) to remember your preferences across sessions. This data stays on your device and is not read or written anywhere else.
privacy.crash.d: The macOS app integrates Sentry crash reporting: only when the app crashes, an anonymous diagnostic report is sent automatically, containing the crash stack, app version, and OS version, to help fix issues. It never contains frame content, files, or personal information. No network requests are made during normal use.
privacy.none.t: No accounts, no analytics, no ads
privacy.none.d: This product contains no analytics, tracking, advertising, or third-party code; there is no account system, no backend server, and no usage data collection.
privacy.changes.d: If this policy changes, the effective date at the top of this page will be updated and the new version published at this address.
privacy.contact.1: Questions about this policy? Email us or open an issue: github.com/gamepunk/magic-mirror

about.title: About
about.p1: Magic Mirror started with a simple idea: the information that matters most on your screen should always be in sight — not hidden in a background tab.
about.p2: We believe a mirroring tool shouldn't come at the cost of privacy. Every frame is processed on your device and never touches a server.
about.p3: Currently maintained by an indie developer — feedback and ideas are always welcome.
about.v2.d: One feature done well beats ten done badly.
